items.title: The fresher paradox: why entry-level jobs ask for 3 years of experience
items.pt:
"Entry-level. 3+ years of experience required." If you are a fresher, you have probably read some version of that line this week.

It is not your imagination. In 2018, a small US job-search company called TalentWorks pulled a random sample of 95,363 job postings and found that 61% of full-time "entry-level" jobs asked for three or more years of experience.

items.title: Post-meeting notes vs live suggestions: which problem each one solves
items.pt:
Two jobs get bundled under meeting tools, and they rarely sit well in the same product.

The first job is a record. Someone needs to know, tomorrow or next month, what was decided, who owns which task, and what was actually said about the deadline. Memory is unreliable, and notes taken while you are also expected to talk get worse as the call runs.

items.title: Common mistakes when reviewing a PR in a java developer interview
items.pt:
Asking a candidate to review a pull request is a good practice in a Java developer interview. Instead of asking theoretical questions whose answers can be memorized, you can discuss working code and real engineering decisions. This makes it easier to see whether the candidate has hands-on experience and how deeply they can analyze someone else’s changes.

items.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
items.pt: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.pt: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction. Simulated participants act from isolated profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, adapting to the agent's speech and tool outcomes. Across

items.title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
items.pt: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are capable low-level controllers, but they tie where objects go to the layouts they were trained on: when objects are moved or obstacles block the way, they carry them to the wrong place or into collisions. Fine-tuning on new layouts needs robot data for each one and erodes skills the model already has. items.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
items.pt: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story. Agent systems provide such memory for offline multi-shot generation, yet they read the whole script in advance, plan each shot before generating it, and regenerate failed shots, which a live stream does not allow.
